intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-12-31). Physics is the science of how things move, interact, and exist, from the tiniest particles inside atoms to the vast galaxies stretching across space. It’s the foundation of modern technology, the reason rockets fly, and the explanation behind everyday phenomena like why your phone works or how a soccer ball curves through the air.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Your patrol rolls two solid spheres of the exact same size and shape down an inclined ramp from rest: one made of aluminum and one made of heavy brass. Neglecting air resistance, how do their accelerations down the ramp compare?
quiz_item.question: Your patrol rolls two solid spheres of the exact same size and shape down an inclined ramp from rest: one made of aluminum and one made of heavy brass. Neglecting air resistance, how do their accelerations down the ramp compare?
options: A. The heavier brass sphere accelerates twice as fast because it has more gravitational mass.
B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
C. The lighter aluminum sphere reaches the bottom first because it has less friction.
D. Neither sphere rolls unless the ramp angle exceeds 45 degrees.
choices: A. The heavier brass sphere accelerates twice as fast because it has more gravitational mass.
B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
C. The lighter aluminum sphere reaches the bottom first because it has less friction.
D. Neither sphere rolls unless the ramp angle exceeds 45 degrees.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Since both gravitational force and moment of inertia are proportional to mass (I = 2/5 m r^2), mass cancels out of the equation of motion on an incline.

quiz_item.question: Which statement best defines the science of physics and how its branches relate to the natural world?
options: A. It is the study of classifying rocks, minerals, and tectonic plate boundaries on Earth.
B. It is the study of how matter and energy interact across space and time, from subatomic particles to the cosmos.
C. It is the practice of mixing chemical reagents to synthesize new plastics and medicines.
D. It is a branch of mathematics that only calculates abstract geometry without testing physical objects.
choices: A. It is the study of classifying rocks, minerals, and tectonic plate boundaries on Earth.
B. It is the study of how matter and energy interact across space and time, from subatomic particles to the cosmos.
C. It is the practice of mixing chemical reagents to synthesize new plastics and medicines.
D. It is a branch of mathematics that only calculates abstract geometry without testing physical objects.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. It is the study of how matter and energy interact across space and time, from subatomic particles to the cosmos.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Physics investigates the fundamental interactions between matter and energy across all scales of space and time, forming the foundation for mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, optics, and quantum science (p. 10).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What happens to energy and matter when a mechanical wave travels across the surface of a quiet pond?
quiz_item.question: What happens to energy and matter when a mechanical wave travels across the surface of a quiet pond?
options: A. Water molecules travel outward from the center all the way to the shoreline at the speed of the wave.
B. Potential energy is destroyed at each wave crest and recreated from nothing at each trough.
C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
D. Gravity stops acting on the water surface until the wave vibrations completely die out.
choices: A. Water molecules travel outward from the center all the way to the shoreline at the speed of the wave.
B. Potential energy is destroyed at each wave crest and recreated from nothing at each trough.
C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
D. Gravity stops acting on the water surface until the wave vibrations completely die out.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Waves transfer energy from one place to another without transporting the bulk matter of the medium, which simply oscillates around its resting position (p. 17).

requirements.req_text: Hands-On Experimentation. Conduct THREE physics experiments, selecting from the following options. Each experiment must include: a hypothesis, materials used, safety precautions, observations, and conclusions based on results. Explain how each experiment demonstrates key physics principles. For each experiment, be sure to try variations/variables to test your hypothesis. (A) Option A: Newton's Laws in Action: Balloon-Powered Car. Make and test a balloon-powered car to show how force and motion interact. (B) Option B: Momentum: Stacked Ball Drop. Drop different-sized stacked balls to show momentum. (C) Option C: Centrifugal Force. Make spinning toys to demonstrate centrifugal force. (D) Option D: Centripetal Force. Swing a water bucket or tray filled with water glasses to demonstrate centripetal force. (E) Option E: Balance. Explore center of gravity, inertia, and harmonic motion using a Tweety Bopper. (F) Option F: Visualize Sound. Visualize Chladni patterns using a tonoscope. (G) Option G: Cartesian Diver. Demonstrate buoyancy and the ideal gas law with Cartesian divers. (H) Option H: Air Pressure: Bernoulli's principle and the Coandă Effect. Balance different objects in a stream of air. (I) Option I: Electromagnet. Make an electromagnet and explore how to increase its strength.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In the Cartesian diver experiment, why does the diver sink to the bottom when you squeeze the sides of the sealed plastic bottle?
quiz_item.question: In the Cartesian diver experiment, why does the diver sink to the bottom when you squeeze the sides of the sealed plastic bottle?
options: A. Squeezing the bottle heats the water, which makes the liquid less dense than the plastic diver.
B. Squeezing creates a magnetic field at the bottom of the bottle that pulls the diver downward.
C. Squeezing removes gravity from the upper half of the bottle and concentrates it at the base.
D. Increased pressure compresses the air pocket inside the diver, increasing its overall density above the density of water.
choices: A. Squeezing the bottle heats the water, which makes the liquid less dense than the plastic diver.
B. Squeezing creates a magnetic field at the bottom of the bottle that pulls the diver downward.
C. Squeezing removes gravity from the upper half of the bottle and concentrates it at the base.
D. Increased pressure compresses the air pocket inside the diver, increasing its overall density above the density of water.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Increased pressure compresses the air pocket inside the diver, increasing its overall density above the density of water.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): By Pascal's principle and the ideal gas law, squeezing the bottle transmits pressure throughout the water and compresses the trapped air bubble, reducing buoyancy so the diver sinks (p. 25).

quiz_item.question: According to the impulse-momentum theorem, how does a collapsible crumple zone keep a raw egg from cracking in the Egg Drop Challenge?
options: A. It increases the mass of the egg at the moment of impact so gravity stops pulling on it.
B. It makes the container bounce upward faster than it hit the ground to double the impact force.
C. It extends the duration of the collision impact, which decreases the peak force acting on the egg shell.
D. It prevents the falling container from gaining any kinetic energy during its descent.
choices: A. It increases the mass of the egg at the moment of impact so gravity stops pulling on it.
B. It makes the container bounce upward faster than it hit the ground to double the impact force.
C. It extends the duration of the collision impact, which decreases the peak force acting on the egg shell.

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. It extends the duration of the collision impact, which decreases the peak force acting on the egg shell.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Because impulse equals force multiplied by time, extending the stopping time with a deformable crumple zone significantly lowers the peak force experienced by the egg (p. 42).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Your patrol rolls two solid spheres of the exact same size and shape down an inclined ramp from rest: one made of aluminum and one made of heavy brass. Neglecting air resistance, how do their accelerations down the ramp compare?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Your patrol rolls two solid spheres of the exact same size and shape down an inclined ramp from rest: one made of aluminum and one made of heavy brass. Neglecting air resistance, how do their accelerations down the ramp compare?
options: A. The heavier brass sphere accelerates twice as fast because it has more gravitational mass.
B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
C. The lighter aluminum sphere reaches the bottom first because it has less friction.
D. Neither sphere rolls unless the ramp angle exceeds 45 degrees.
choices: A. The heavier brass sphere accelerates twice as fast because it has more gravitational mass.
B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
C. The lighter aluminum sphere reaches the bottom first because it has less friction.
D. Neither sphere rolls unless the ramp angle exceeds 45 degrees.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Since both gravitational force and moment of inertia are proportional to mass (I = 2/5 m r^2), mass cancels out of the equation of motion on an incline.

choices: A. It is the study of classifying rocks, minerals, and tectonic plate boundaries on Earth.
B. It is the study of how matter and energy interact across space and time, from subatomic particles to the cosmos.
C. It is the practice of mixing chemical reagents to synthesize new plastics and medicines.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It is the study of how matter and energy interact across space and time, from subatomic particles to the cosmos.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Physics investigates the fundamental interactions between matter and energy across all scales of space and time, forming the foundation for mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, optics, and quantum science (p. 10).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens to energy and matter when a mechanical wave travels across the surface of a quiet pond?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens to energy and matter when a mechanical wave travels across the surface of a quiet pond?
options: A. Water molecules travel outward from the center all the way to the shoreline at the speed of the wave.
B. Potential energy is destroyed at each wave crest and recreated from nothing at each trough.
C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
D. Gravity stops acting on the water surface until the wave vibrations completely die out.
choices: A. Water molecules travel outward from the center all the way to the shoreline at the speed of the wave.
B. Potential energy is destroyed at each wave crest and recreated from nothing at each trough.
C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
D. Gravity stops acting on the water surface until the wave vibrations completely die out.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Waves transfer energy from one place to another without transporting the bulk matter of the medium, which simply oscillates around its resting position (p. 17).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In the Cartesian diver experiment, why does the diver sink to the bottom when you squeeze the sides of the sealed plastic bottle?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In the Cartesian diver experiment, why does the diver sink to the bottom when you squeeze the sides of the sealed plastic bottle?
options: A. Squeezing the bottle heats the water, which makes the liquid less dense than the plastic diver.
B. Squeezing creates a magnetic field at the bottom of the bottle that pulls the diver downward.
C. Squeezing removes gravity from the upper half of the bottle and concentrates it at the base.
D. Increased pressure compresses the air pocket inside the diver, increasing its overall density above the density of water.
choices: A. Squeezing the bottle heats the water, which makes the liquid less dense than the plastic diver.
B. Squeezing creates a magnetic field at the bottom of the bottle that pulls the diver downward.
C. Squeezing removes gravity from the upper half of the bottle and concentrates it at the base.
D. Increased pressure compresses the air pocket inside the diver, increasing its overall density above the density of water.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Increased pressure compresses the air pocket inside the diver, increasing its overall density above the density of water.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): By Pascal's principle and the ideal gas law, squeezing the bottle transmits pressure throughout the water and compresses the trapped air bubble, reducing buoyancy so the diver sinks (p. 25).

B. It eliminates gravitational potential energy so the timber weighs less at the top of the lift.

choices: A. It multiplies mechanical advantage so Scouts pull with less force over a longer rope distance while conserving total work.
B. It eliminates gravitational potential energy so the timber weighs less at the top of the lift.
C. It creates extra mechanical energy inside the pulley wheels so less rope needs to be pulled.
D. It converts static friction directly into upward magnetic lift along the hemp rope.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. It multiplies mechanical advantage so Scouts pull with less force over a longer rope distance while conserving total work.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): A pulley system provides mechanical advantage by distributing the load across multiple supporting rope segments, reducing required effort force while increasing pull distance (p. 32).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the impulse-momentum theorem, how does a collapsible crumple zone keep a raw egg from cracking in the Egg Drop Challenge?
options: A. It increases the mass of the egg at the moment of impact so gravity stops pulling on it.
B. It makes the container bounce upward faster than it hit the ground to double the impact force.
C. It extends the duration of the collision impact, which decreases the peak force acting on the egg shell.
D. It prevents the falling container from gaining any kinetic energy during its descent.
choices: A. It increases the mass of the egg at the moment of impact so gravity stops pulling on it.
B. It makes the container bounce upward faster than it hit the ground to double the impact force.
C. It extends the duration of the collision impact, which decreases the peak force acting on the egg shell.
D. It prevents the falling container from gaining any kinetic energy during its descent.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. It extends the duration of the collision impact, which decreases the peak force acting on the egg shell.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Because impulse equals force multiplied by time, extending the stopping time with a deformable crumple zone significantly lowers the peak force experienced by the egg (p. 42).
